notable_absence.finding: As in the Capella twin, the rearm call happens at the top of the callback specifically so recurrence survives errors or timeouts in the callback's own later logic - there is no retry-count limit, backoff policy, or failure-alerting concept named anywhere on this page. This Server page's cleanup note reveals a naming inconsistency the Capella twin has no equivalent for: it instructs the reader to undeploy a Function named 'cancel_overwrite_timer' even though this page's actual example is named 'recurring_timer' throughout - 'Go to the Eventing portion of the UI and undeploy the Function **cancel\_overwrite\_timer**' - apparently copy-pasted cleanup boilerplate from the sibling cancel-overwrite-timer page that was never corrected to match this page's own Function name.

cross_product_finding: Confirms the classic-role requirement (Full Admin / Eventing Full Admin via Function Scope) found on every other worked-example page in this batch, absent from the Capella twin. This is also the page the round 18 context specifically flagged as containing an unquotable behavesDifferentlyUnder relation in the Capella twin's own record (verify-evidence.py finding) - the Server page states the identical active/inactive branching fact with directly quotable, verbatim evidence, so the underlying fact is confirmed true and now properly evidenced rather than resting on the Capella extraction's word alone.
